Methods: We introduce a grounded retrieval method that filters passages before generation.
Datasets: We evaluate the method on a small scientific question answering benchmark.
Results: The method improves evidence recall and reduces unsupported answers compared with a lexical baseline.
Limitations: The method fails when the corpus contains no relevant evidence.

Methods: We apply a cross-encoder reranker after first-stage retrieval.
Datasets: Experiments use noisy web and scientific document collections.
Results: Reranking improves precision but cannot improve accuracy on queries with missing evidence.
Limitations: The reranker adds latency and depends on a domain-matched training distribution.

title: Evaluating Research Agents with Citation Audits

Methods: We define claim-evidence pairs and audit citations before report completion.
Datasets: The evaluation contains multi-paper research questions and manually labeled evidence.
Results: Citation audits identify unsupported claims and expose conflicts between papers.
Limitations: Human labels remain necessary for entailment and report readability evaluation.
